locations.quote: **Since** some Version Control (VC) systems include a Continuous Integration (CI) application, it is possible to reduce the effort required to maintain the servers and migrate the CI service from external applications as Jenkins to the inbuilt CI service.

**To achieve** this goal, Artemis uses a Version Control (VC) and Continuous Integration (CI) server, to execute test cases predefined by the instructor on each submission of each student, display the build results and grade the submission [Krusche18].
**In order to implement** this idea, the lecture is split up into multiple iterations, each consisting of different phases [Krusche17].
**As a result**, instructors are able to update the build plan after the release of an exercise, GitLab CI fetches the updated build plan when needed.
**Since** CI services are now often included with VC servers, it is now possible to migrate external CI servers as Jenkins to GitLab CI and so reduce additional work for server administration.

**Since** the benefits of using CI are quite high and nearly half of the developers who do not use CI mention a lack of familiarity as the reason for not using a CI service, it is useful to teach the concepts of CI at university [Hilton16].
**As described** in section 3, this might lead to better developers and better code, due to the fact, that more students will be taught the concepts of CI.

locations.quote: **Furthermore**, it should be possible to adjust the build plan after the task has been assigned.
This leads to **additional** server overhead, since the CI and the Version Control (VC) are running on different servers.
**Additionally**, the base build plan is copied once after the student started the exercise [Krusche18].
Not only projects using CI release twice as often as projects without CI, but the build is **also** less likely to fail in the master branch [Hilton16].
**In addition**, universities will save time and money as they will need at least one less server.
**In addition**, either Ansible or a Kubernetes cluster can be used for automatic deployment of the GitLab CI Runners.
